prompt:
Bug: translating an AI-imported recipe loses its servings and yield quantity, and pages already in the target language get translated anyway.

When an import asks for a translation (WorkflowOptions.translate_language), TranslateRecipeStep sends the draft recipe to the AI provider and cleans the answer again.

1. Numbers lost. The draft's yield is already split into numbers (recipe_servings, recipe_yield_quantity) and wording (recipe_yield). Only the wording goes to the provider, so once the answer is cleaned again both numbers are 0. Expected: after TranslateRecipeStep.run the recipe keeps the draft's recipe_servings and recipe_yield_quantity, while recipe_yield takes the translated wording and the name and other fields come from the translation. A draft with yield "4 servings" (servings 4) translated with no yield ends with servings 4 and quantity 0. A draft "12 Stücke" (quantity 12, yield "Stücke") translated as "pieces" ends with quantity 12, yield "pieces", servings 0. Structured times carry over as today (total_time_seconds 600 for PT10M).

2. Language check. should_run compares the target with the compiled source's language as raw strings, so "de-DE" and "German" count as different. Add a module-level function language_code(language) next to TranslateRecipeStep (the tests import both from the same module). It returns a language's two- or three-letter code in lower case, or None:
- a tag of two or three letters, optionally followed by parts after "-" or "_": "de", "DE", "de-DE" and "de_de" give "de";
- a language name from LOCALE_CONFIG, the code being the first part of its key ("de-DE" gives "de"): either half of "Deutsch (German)", so "German" and "Deutsch" give "de"; "Brazilian Portuguese" gives "pt". A single word of a name counts too when it belongs to one language only: "English" (American English, British English) gives "en", "Chinese" gives "zh";
- case and surrounding spaces are ignored (" german " gives "de"); "Klingon", "" and None give None.
should_run then skips the translation when both sides have the same code: target "de-DE" with source "German", "Deutsch" or "de"; "en-US" with "English"; "en-GB" with "en-US". It runs for another language ("en-US" with "German", "de-DE" with "fr-FR") and when the source language is None or not recognized ("Klingon"), since such a source may be in any language. If either side is not recognized, the two values are compared as text, ignoring case and surrounding spaces. Without a target language it never runs.

3. Page language. StructuredDataCompiler.compile always reports language None. For HTML input it should report the lang attribute of the <html> element, trimmed and otherwise as written: lang="de" gives "de", lang=" de-DE " gives "de-DE", an empty or missing lang gives None. JSON and plain-text input stay None.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit_tests/services_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).
title: fix: keep servings and yield quantity when translating AI-imported recipes (#8636)
